meta.title: Rice visualisation constants
meta.description: Physical constants used to turn money into grains, bowls, sacks and heaps of rice.

grain_weight_g.source: U.S. Patent 10,624,292 (Rice cultivar M-210, California Cooperative Rice Research Foundation): 1000-grain weight of milled rice 21.65 g
grain_weight_g.definition: Mass of one grain of milled white rice, taken as the 1000-grain weight of a typical medium-grain cultivar divided by 1000 (21.65 g / 1000). Grain weights of milled rice vary by variety, roughly 15–30 mg per grain; Humphrey Yang's original measurement (58 lb for 1.22 million grains) implies about 21.6 mg per grain, which matches this value.
grain_weight_g.estimate_by: Cultivar-specific laboratory value used as a typical grain weight

bowl_weight_g.source: Definition used by this site (no external source needed): one bowl = 200 g of uncooked rice
bowl_weight_g.definition: Convention chosen for the visualisation: a rice bowl holds 200 g of uncooked rice. This is a unit definition, not an empirical claim.

sack_weight_g.source: Definition used by this site: one sack = 25 kg, a common trade sack size for rice
sack_weight_g.definition: Convention chosen for the visualisation: a sack holds 25 kg of rice. This is a unit definition, not an empirical claim.

truck_weight_g.source: Definition used by this site: one truckload = 25 t (typical payload of a 40-t articulated lorry)
truck_weight_g.definition: Convention chosen for the visualisation: a truckload is 25 tonnes of rice. This is a unit definition, not an empirical claim.
